featured_reviews.name: Rahul Kalyan Revankar
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited this place atleast 2-3 times in the last 2-3 months with family and friends. Trust me, it truly made me feel like that I am having homemade sea food. There ambience has been good.I tried relishing their pomfret, king mackerel and bombil thali, it's all amazing. Quantity they serve is really good. Staff is very polite and they helps you with an option about what to choose from their speciality.. though I didn't try their chicken dishes yet, but they serve amazing bombil potli, prawns potli,mandeli potli and mutton potli. Prices wise also it is very friendly. Over all I had a very good experience visiting this place. Going there early in the evening at around 7:30-8pm is preferrable even on the weekends when all the sea food lovers try and cash on too. Because the place is very tiny. As there are hardly 8-10 tables but they have a huge kitchen. Majority of the sea food lovers prefer ordering food from Zomato or Swiggy . Staff really makes you feel comfortable at all times. If you are a true sea food lover and staying near by in borivli and dahisar then this one is a must visit place. It's located in the heart of IC colony at holy cross road and at 5 minutes walking distance from mandapeshwar/IC colony metro station, near Studio Fernandes,St Thomas Church Road.

featured_reviews.name: Ameya Banavali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience on Diwali day!!
Pity the owners because the server threatened customers that they will hit them and the owners would not say anything

Detailed review
I visited today at 1:50 pm. There were people in waiting outside.
After waiting for 6 minutes, a server came out to inform that there was a notebook kept at the side which the customer had to note down their booking by themselves for (no staff to do this)

After waiting for half an hour in the sweltering heat, we (myself, wife and father in law ) got a seat at the further most corner. The one and only AC in the place was running at full throttle but it failed to provide cooling to the crowded room full of customers.

We had already chosen our choice of orders during our wait outside.

Order for :
- Mutton Thali
- Extra Chapati
- Extra Bhakri
- Bombil Fry
- Chicken Poppers
- Alani Bhaat
- Thumbs up half ltr.

After waiting for another 10 mins seated on the table, the server (same guy as earlier) came and took our order very efficiently. 👍

This was at around 2:30 pm. As it was too late for lunch already, we instructed the waiter to get our orders as soon as they were prepared.

The server promptly got the coldrink and plonked the bottle on the table without serving and left. Then we waited and waited and waited.... And waited some more....
In-between we asked the waiter 5 times about when we could see some food on our table his reply everytime was " bas aa rahaa hai"

So after waiting till 3 pm after my senior citizen father in law started getting agitated, (by this time the bombil had been served to us by a lady). At this point I asked the waiter in a loud voice about rest  of my order, The moment I raised my voice, the waiter started shouting back and threatened to hit me.

When the matter escalated, another guy, seemingly the owner came to our table to sort out the matter , he confessed theybwere short on staff  today (not my problem but still)

The lady also intervened and then on she cooled the situation with prompt service and the required attention.

On the food front
Bombil were oily
Mutton was chewy
Poppers were good
Alani Bhaat was excellent

Trigger points-
- This hotel doesnt even have a working washbasin for customers to rinse post meal. Please bear in mind that these people serve fish.
- The AC is pathetic which brings upon a strange discomfort while eating.
- An uncle is a safari suit who was from the restaurant team and claimed be from some food department told that everything is made fresh.  This explains the chewy undercooked mutton as you need to cook mutton for atleast an hour, and simmer before dishing it out.
-Total bill was 1780.

Post meal review-
- At the time of writing this detailed review I am feeling acidic reflux and so is my wife which indicates the quality of ingredients used.

Dear owners
- Your food is pathetic.
- Your ambience is meh.
- Not to be classist but your service is good probably for the slums, not IC Colony.

P.S. I have also messaged my friend who recommended your restaurant to stay away henceforth.

Happy Diwali!

featured_reviews.name: THE SIMPLE SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text:
A jewel worth your moolah! Nestled in the by-lanes of Borivali, this little gem is a sparkler, for sure. Your search for authentic Malvani cuisine ends here.
Be it the use of spices, the freshness of the ingredients, the quantity, the quality and the authenticity...all scream 'Fantastic'!
The thalis are delicious and freshly prepared. They do not scrimp on the fried fish or prawns. In fact, on offer, is a free side of freshly fried bombils with the fish thalis and free kothimbir wadi with the Veg thali on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
The fish is fresh. The solkadi is yummy. The JOWARI BHAKRI is super soft..😋
The Kothimbir wadis are delightful too.
The fish gravy is a tad spicy...not for the faint-hearted. But just the way Malvani cuisine should be.
The fresh lime soda is decent.
The absolute highlight: The modaks, though it was a 20 minute wait.  Fresh. Authentic. Mouth-watering, to say the least. And the drizzle of ghee over the modaks...👌😋😋...oohhlaalaa..next level. A++
The juiciest, most scrumptious modaks you could ever have  eaten.
Definitely worth a return...over and over. If consistency prevails.
Thumbs up!! 👍👌

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since we were craving seafood for dinner, I decided to visit Konkan Kinara with my family. The restaurant had a minimalistic setup. When we arrived around 10:45 PM on a Friday night, the place was almost empty, with just one other table occupied. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, going by the name, I assumed they specialized only in Konkani cuisine. But to my surprise, they also served North Indian and Chinese dishes.

To start our meal, we ordered Manchow Soup. Then, we tried Bombil Fry, which was disappointing. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, I expected the fish to be well-marinated, but it tasted bland. So, I had to ask them to take it away. They were kind enough to serve it again, and this time, the flavors were much better.

Next, we tried Veg Seekh Kebab, which had a nice earthy flavor. The Orange Mojito was fresh and had a unique orange flavor. Then, we ordered Masala Papad, Chicken Thali, Mutton Thali, and Veg Thali. The masala papad was crispy and flavorful. The thalis were wholesome, and I feel one thali is more than enough for one person. With every thali, you have the option to choose between Bhakri, Chapati, or Wade, which adds a nice customization to the meal.

I especially liked the Chicken Thali, which came with bhakri. The bhakri was so soft, and I could tell from the taste that it was freshly made. The Veg Thali was also sufficient and included a sweet dish. To end the meal, we ordered Caramel Custard, which was delicious and properly made.

The staff was polite, but at times, they seemed more focused on watching a cricket match rather than attending to guests. We had to call them multiple times for basic service, like refilling water or checking on our order. A little more attentiveness would have made the experience much better.

The restaurant seemed hygienic to me, and overall, it was a decent experience at Konkan Kinara. If you are in the mood for a meat thali or seafood, you may consider visiting this place.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pangat is one of those places you walk into with high expectations, especially given its reputation for Malvani thalis and coastal favourites. Having been regular patrons for many years, this place has held a certain nostalgic charm for us, which made our recent visits all the more noticeable in contrast.
We sampled a fairly elaborate spread, including their Bombil Thali, Surmai Thali, Prawns Thali, Mandeli fry, along with add ons like the much talked about Crab Lollypop, Bheja Masala, Kalva Sukka, Chicken Potli Kebab, and also revisited dishes we have enjoyed in the past like the keema pattice, bombil fry, and mutton masala.
While the menu continues to promise a seafood lover’s delight, the overall experience, unfortunately, felt average this time around. The Bombil and Surmai fry had the expected crispness, but lacked that depth of flavour and freshness that truly elevates coastal cuisine. The curries across thalis felt somewhat one dimensional, missing the robust, layered Malvani masala profile one associates with Pangat. Even the basics like chapatis and bhakris, which form the backbone of such meals, could be softer, fresher, and more refined.
On a more specific note, the tisrya masala (dry) felt quite chewy, almost rubbery in texture, taking away from what is otherwise a delightful dish when done right. The solkadhi, too, seemed to miss that refreshing kokam forward tang we have experienced here earlier and elsewhere.
That said, what truly stood out and deserves full credit was the service and hospitality. The staff handled everything with genuine warmth, attentiveness, and honesty. From guiding through the menu to ensuring timely service, their effort and intent were clearly heartfelt, and it did make a meaningful difference to the overall dining experience.
Pangat certainly has the foundation of a great dining destination, and perhaps it is just a matter of revisiting the fundamentals. With a bit more attention to core elements like breads, curries, and flavour balance, it has every potential to regain the consistency and charm it was once known for.
For now, a place that still offers variety, but one we hope will soon rediscover the flavours that made it special for us over the years.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
It has been more than twenty years since I first visited Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar with my family, and it continues to remain a special place for us in Borivali. It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

Ratings:
Quality - 4/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 4.2/5
Price - ₹5000 for 8 people

featured_reviews.name: Ankit Latam
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently tried a Malvani Pahunchar restaurant and ordered a chicken platter, chicken dish, prawns, and a bombil thali — and it turned out to be a proper coastal feast.
The chicken platter was generous and full of bold Malvani flavors. The spices were rich without overpowering the natural taste, and every bite had that smoky, masala-coated goodness. The chicken dish itself was cooked beautifully — tender, juicy, and soaked in a thick, aromatic gravy that paired perfectly with bhakri.
The prawns were the highlight for seafood lovers. Fresh, succulent, and cooked just right, they carried that authentic coastal spice blend that hits you with warmth rather than heat. And the bombil thali felt like a complete experience — crispy bombil, flavorful curry, and comforting sides that balanced everything out.
Overall, the meal felt homely yet indulgent — exactly what you hope for when craving Malvani cuisine. If you enjoy bold spices, fresh seafood, and hearty portions, this place definitely delivers.

customer_updates.text:
I recently experienced Comfort Kitchen with friends for the first time, and the ambiance was notably inviting, offering a cozy atmosphere that proved to be perfect for photography, adorned with wall paneling that contributed to an opulent environment.

Our culinary choices included the Mushroom Cream Soup as a starter, which impressed with its creamy and delicious texture, evoking a heartwarming sensation, earning a perfect 5/5 rating.

The Deconstructed Chicken Shashlik arrived as four skewers of impeccably cooked chicken, accompanied by Szechuan sauce, mayo-based sauce, and a garnish of cilantro basil herbs, sprinkled with sesame seeds. The chicken exhibited perfection, being both juicy and tender, making it a highly recommended dish with a rating of 4/5.

On the other hand, the Crispy Chicken, consisting of cornflake-coated chicken breast pieces, served with tartar sauce and wasabi mayo, left room for improvement. The thin chicken breast pieces were unfortunately overcooked, resulting in dryness. Additionally, the misidentification of the wasabi mayo as homemade mint herb mayo contributed to a less favorable experience, warranting a 2/5 rating.

That said, a couple of items were served cold, which took away from the overall experience a bit. Hopefully, that’s something they can improve on.

If you’re looking for a peaceful place with a wide range of food options, it’s still worth a visit!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Sunday The Comfort Kitchen in Borivali, and I must say it was a delightful experience from start to finish.

The ambiance was warm and inviting, creating the perfect atmosphere for a relaxed meal. The restaurant's decor exuded a cozy charm that instantly put me at ease.

Now, let's talk about the food. The menu offered a variety of options, and I was truly impressed by the diverse range of dishes they had to offer. The flavors were rich and authentic, and every bite felt like a burst of happiness in my mouth.

The service was top-notch. The staff was attentive, friendly, and always ready to assist with any questions or recommendations. It's evident that the team at Sunday takes great pride in ensuring their guests have a memorable dining experience.

In terms of value, the prices were reasonable for the quality and quantity of food served. Dining here felt like a great value for money.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Sunday - The Comfort Kitchen, Borivali for a dinner date with my husband.
And..oh my God - the two of us experienced the 'Ratatouille-effect' as soon as we took our first bite!! Our taste buds tingled and danced with absolute joy. The food was hands-down, undoubtedly savoury and scrumptious.
So we ordered - Prawns Papped & Chicken Cigars for starters, followed by Non-Veg Dragon's Delight Sizzler as our main. A big big 👍🏻 for the way the chef handled each of the proteins in all our dishes. Both chicken and prawns were cooked to perfection! The dishes were not only a feast for the eyes but they were very well-seasoned, lip-smacking & as the name of this restaurant goes -- 'TOTALLY COMFORTING'.
I would highly recommend this place to all.
Will soon be returning - hungry to gobble more 🫶🏻
